angle: Arsenal let him go as a boy, Spurs' own youth coach says he 'wasn't even on the podium' of his age group, and he was shipped out on four loans. In 2026 he became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.
why_now: In the news this month: Ballon d'Or (26 Oct), new Bayern contract to 2029 (5 Nov), England's most-capped men's player with his 126th cap v Croatia (12 Nov), and on the five-man shortlist for the first BBC Men's Footballer of the Year, voting open until 27 Nov (BBC Sport, 19 Nov). open_loop: Arsenal let him go as a boy. In October he won the Ballon d'Or. How did the kid nobody picked end up the best player in the world?

beats.fact: Harry Kane was rejected by Arsenal's academy as a boy. In October 2026 he won the Ballon d'Or, the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001.

Even at Tottenham's academy he was not seen as a future star. (Voice, max 12 words: 'Even Spurs' youth coach didn't rate him top of his group.') His former Spurs youth coach Alex Inglethorpe said he 'probably wasn't even on the podium' of his age group.
beats.quote: I'd like to say he was the gold medallist in the group and we'd all spotted he was going to be the fantastic player, but I'd be lying. He probably wasn't even on the podium.

sources.outlet: The Guardian ("Kane was never a wonderkid at Spurs")
The Guardian ("He was unexceptional as a junior")

beats.fact: Spurs sent him out on four loans: Leyton Orient (5 goals in 18 games, 2011), Millwall (9 goals, 2012), then Norwich and Leicester.
Last season he scored 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern, the most a Bayern player has scored in a season, and 73 for club and country. Then the Ballon d'Or, and his own verdict on the journey.
beats.quote: I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now.

sources.outlet: The Guardian (61 for Bayern, 12 for England)

beats.fact: Kane has 156 goals in 161 games for Bayern, has signed a new contract to 2029, and on 12 November won his 126th England cap, passing Peter Shilton as England's most-capped men's player. He scored in that game.
